sentences.text: Revenue, net interest income plus noninterest income, rose from $96.6 billion in FY2016 to $182 billion in FY2025, a 7.3% CAGR [D5][D206].
Net income compounded at 9.7% and diluted EPS at 13.9% over the same window [F113][F115].
The shape is a step change, not a smooth compound: revenue grew 1.4% in FY2021, then 22.9% in FY2023 and 12.3% in FY2024 [D129][D179][D202].
The FY2023 step came from net interest income, up 33.8%, as higher rates lifted interest income to $170.6 billion [D174][X125][P36].
FY2025 growth slowed to 2.8% as net interest income rose 3.1% and noninterest income 2.4% [D226][D221][D222].
North America supplied 76.6% of FY2025 revenue but only 0.2pp of its growth, while EMEA and Asia-Pacific contributed 1.2pp each [D249][D251][D276][D301].
Asia-Pacific was the fastest-growing geography at 17.3% in FY2025, versus 0.3% for North America [D300][D250].
FY2025 net interest income growth was driven by higher Markets net interest income and higher revolving balances in Card Services, largely offset by deposit margin compression [P28].
Noninterest expense grew 4.2% against 2.8% revenue growth, so the efficiency ratio rose to 52.4% from 51.7% [D225][D226][D207][D184].
EPS grew 1.4% while net income fell 2.6%, as the diluted share count fell 3.4% [D216][D214][D224].
The FY2025 efficiency ratio of 52.4% sits below the window median of 57.2% and above the FY2024 low of 51.7% [D207][D333][D331].
It is far better than the banks peer median of 61.7%, ranking at the 0th percentile where lower is better [D336][D337].
The FY2025 expense increase came from higher compensation, brokerage and distribution fees, auto lease depreciation, technology and marketing, partly offset by FDIC special assessment releases [P26].
The credit-loss provision rose to 7.8% of revenue from 6.0%, above the peer median of 6.0% [D208][D185][D341].
The FY2025 provision reflected portfolio growth, client-specific credit changes, updated leveraged-loan loss assumptions and estimated borrower-fraud losses [P15].
Operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure for a bank; FY2025 operating cash flow was -$147.8 billion against $57.0 billion of net income [F60][F30].
The FY2025 outflow came from higher trading assets, securities borrowed, loan originations and other assets, partly offset by net income and higher trading liabilities [P21].
Capital return is the better test: buybacks plus dividends of $48.2 billion equaled 84.6% of FY2025 net income [D205][F30].
Return on average equity was 16.1% in FY2025, against a banks peer median of 11.8% and a 100th-percentile rank [D213][D339][D338].
Loans were 57.3% of deposits, up from 55.0%, as loans grew to $1.47 trillion and deposits to $2.56 trillion [D211][D188][X197][X207].
The loan growth was driven by CIB Markets and securities-based lending in AWM on higher client demand [P4].
Shareholders' equity rose 5.1% to $362 billion while buybacks reached $31.6 billion, and the diluted share count fell 3.4% [D220][F110][X102][D224].
Net income for FY2021 through FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy pay-versus-performance table, not the 10-K, and differs by up to 0.10% [R1][F26][X16][F30][X20].
The gap is immaterial to ratios but matters where precision is claimed, so the 10-K figures should be used [R1].
FY2020 pretax income and tax expense were later restated, and the pack uses the first-reported values [R2][R3][X63][X73].
Criticized wholesale exposure rose to $48.5 billion from $44.7 billion, though it fell to 3.4% of wholesale credit exposure from 3.5% [P2].
If the efficiency ratio rises above the FY2024 low of 51.7%, the cost trend described here would reverse [D331].
If the credit-loss provision exceeds 7.8% of revenue, credit costs would be worsening from the FY2025 level [D208].
If net interest income growth falls below the FY2025 3.1%, the deposit margin compression cited in the FY2025 10-K would be outweighing balance growth [D221][P28].
